news.title: World Cup boss mutually terminates contract after resignation speculation
news.lede: The 73-year-old had seemingly announced his resignation following the Black Stars' World Cup exit in July. Ghana crashed out in the Round of 32 - losing 1-0 to Colombia - with Queiroz taking to social media where he appeared to confirm his departure. Having taken charge of the African nation in April, his four-month contract was set to expire following the conclusion of the global tournament. But just days after his statement, the ex-Manchester United assistant manager denied his exit, insisting his post was purely a 'message of gratitude'.

news.title: Yemen and football in the face of civil war: ‘It would be very nice to give the world a different headline’
news.lede: Noureddine Ould Ali is staying positive despite a difficult situation at home and tough opponents at the Gulf Cup. The Yemen national team coach, Noureddine Ould Ali, chose not to reach for a good old-fashioned football excuse for his team’s 1-0 loss to Qatar in the Gulf Cup on Saturday, despite a clear penalty that was not given his way. The defeat meant the Reds crashed out of the eight-nation regional tournament, currently taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with a game of the group stage still remaining. There are other factors that the Algerian coach could list for a defeat against a team that was at the World Cup in the summer.

news.title: Infantino loses Swiss backing for campaign to remain Fifa chief
news.lede: Gianni Infantino's drive to remain boss at world football's governing body Fifa was under threat on Thursday after his own country's football association withdrew its support. Issued on: 01/10/2026 - 15:04Modified: 01/10/2026 - 15:06. Swiss-born Infantino was elected Fifa president in February 2016 and had been expected to sweep to a fourth and final term at elections next March, until a failed bid to allow private investment in the World Cup drew calls for reform. The Swiss Football Association (ASF), one of Fifa's founding members in Paris in 1904, said in June that it would support Infantino.

news.title: Portugal apparently expected Ronaldo to retire after the World Cup—and is now reassigning his jersey number
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has unexpectedly left the Portuguese national team's training camp. According to media reports, the news apparently did not come out of the blue. The federation is said to have been preparing for a future without its superstar for some time.

news.title: United States lined up to host first Women’s Club World Cup
news.lede: LA and San Diego among favoured host cities for 2028. Tournament would include nineteen teams. The United States is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

news.title: Ghana part ways with coach Queiroz after poor start to AFCON qualifiers
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Round of 32 - Colombia v Ghana - Kansas City Stadium, Kansas City, Missouri, U.S. - July 3, 2026 Ghana coach Carlos Queiroz looks dejected REUTERS/Siphiwe Sibeko/File Photo. Oct 1 - Ghana have parted ways with coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent after opening their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations campaign with a pair of defeats, officials said on Thursday. • Ghana lost their first two Cup of Nations qualifiers 2-0 away to Ivory Coast and 4-2 at home to Gambia. • Queiroz, 73, took over in April to lead the team at the World Cup on a short-term contract.

news.title: The Women's Champions League stars giving back to grassroots football
news.lede: The UEFA Women's Champions League's biggest stars began their football journeys in the same way as millions of young people across Europe – playing with friends, joining local teams and taking every opportunity to kick a ball. For Arsenal's Alessia Russo, Chelsea's Keira Walsh, Bayern München's Pernille Harder and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor, those early experiences helped shape careers that have taken them to the highest level of the women's game. Now, all four are giving back to grassroots football, having set up initiatives designed to create more opportunities for young players and inspire the next generation. During UEFA Grassroots Week, they reflect on where their own journeys began, why they wanted to give something back and their advice to young players today.

news.title: Surprise: Ronaldo considered retiring from international football after the World Cup, and Jesus convinced him to complete the journey!
news.lede: The 30-minute promise sparks the crisis between Ronaldo and Jesus. Portuguese journalist Nuno Luz has lifted the lid on the crisis between national team captain Cristiano Ronaldo and head coach Jorge Jesus, revealing the details of the emergency meeting called to settle the dispute. It all started when Ronaldo spent the entire recent match against Norway on Portugal's substitutes' bench. Portugal won the UEFA Nations League clash 2-1, but their absence from the pitch left the Al-Nassr captain furious.
